'''Hiroaki Suga''' ({{nihongo2|菅 裕明}}, born February 21, 1963) is a Japanese biochemist and businessman. He is best known for his work on artificial [[ribozymes]] (flexizymes) and their application in [[mRNA display]] (RaPID, random nonstandard peptide integrated discovery).{{r|wolfprize}}{{r|chemviews}}

Suga was awarded the 2023 [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]], jointly with [[Chuan He]] and [[Jeffery W. Kelly]], "for pioneering discoveries that illuminate the functions and pathological dysfunctions of [[RNA]] and [[proteins]] and for creating strategies to harness the capabilities of these biopolymers in new ways to ameliorate human diseases."{{r|wolfprize}}

==Education ==
Suga graduated from [[Okayama University]] (BSc, MSc) in engineering,{{r|wolfprize}}{{r|sugabio}} and studied at [[University of Lausanne]], where he worked with {{interlanguage link|Manfred Schlosser|de}}.{{r|sugabio}}

Suga completed his Ph.D. in chemistry at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1994 with {{ill|Satoru Masamune|jp|正宗悟}},{{r|sugabio}} working on catalytic [[antibodies]]{{r|sugathesis}}

==Career==
===Scientific===
After graduating from [[MIT]] with a Ph.D., Suga was a [[postdoctoral]] researcher at the [[Jack W. Szostak]] lab of [[Harvard Medical School]] before starting his independent career at [[University at Buffalo]]. Since 2003 he is a faculty member at the [[University of Tokyo]].{{r|sugabio}}

===Business===
Suga is also a founder of PeptiDream Inc. Tokyo, a publicly traded biopharmaceutical start-up company responsible for discovering and developing non-standard peptide therapeutics in addition to addressing unmet medical needs as well as investigating peptide drug conjugates (PDC), peptides, and small molecule-based drugs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2018 |title=Prof. Dr. Hiroaki Suga: The pseudo-natural peptides therapeutic innovation |url=https://www.grk2062.uni-muenchen.de/news-events/suga_talk/index.html |website=Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Hiroaki Suga |url=https://www.horizons-molbio.de/about-1/past-speakers-profiles/hiroaki-suga/ |access-date=2023-03-16 |archive-date=2023-03-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316234219/https://www.horizons-molbio.de/about-1/past-speakers-profiles/hiroaki-suga/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 11, 2022 |title=Current Lecturer |url=https://chab.ethz.ch/en/research/awards-and-lectures/prelog-lecture/current-lecturer.html |access-date=June 21, 2023 |archive-date=August 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829080232/https://chab.ethz.ch/en/research/awards-and-lectures/prelog-lecture/current-lecturer.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> It is traded publicly on the Tokyo First Stock Exchange Market (the market capitalization is over JY 600 billions), which has many partnerships with pharmaceutical companies in worldwide.{{r|chemviews}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 14, 2016 |title=Hiroaki Suga, Professor, University of Tokyo |url= https://nccr-chembio.ch/blog/hiroaki-suga/ |website=Swiss National Center of Competence in Research}}</ref>

Suga is chair of the [[editorial board]] at RSC Chemical Biology{{r|rscchembiol}} and associate editor at [[Angewandte Chemie]].{{r|chemviews}}

==Publications==
Suga has published over 250 scientific articles;{{r|sugapubs}} a small selection is presented here:

*{{cite journal|pages=28–33|doi=10.1038/71225|title=Ribozyme-catalyzed tRNA aminoacylation|year=2000|last1=Lee|first1=Nick|journal=Nature Structural Biology|volume=7|first2=Yoshitaka|last2=Bessho|first3=Kenneth|last3=Wei|first4=Jack W.|last4=Szostak|first5=Hiroaki|last5=Suga|issue=1 |pmid=10625423 |s2cid=1831912 }}
*{{cite journal |pages=11454–11455 |title=Designer Ribozymes: Programming the tRNA Specificity into Flexizyme |year=2004 |last1=Ramaswamy |first1=Krishna |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=126 |issue=37 |last2=Saito |first2=Hirohide |last3=Murakami |first3=Hiroshi |last4=Shiba |first4=Kiyotaka |last5=Suga |first5=Hiroaki |doi=10.1021/ja046843y |pmid=15366888 |bibcode=2004JAChS.12611454R }}
*{{cite journal |pages=1931–1940 |doi=10.1039/C6CC06951G |title=A RaPID way to discover nonstandard macrocyclic peptide modulators of drug targets|year=2017 |last1=Passioura |first1=Toby |journal=Chemical Communications |volume=53 |last2=Suga |first2=Hiroaki|issue=12 |pmid=28091672 }}
